identities.AGENCY_BILLING: A member of the agency that may see billing (quotes, orders, refunds, billing profile). The exact roles are Order 15's; today GetQuote and GetPaymentOrder use AGENCY_READER.
identities.SELLER: A seller reading or acting on their own records only: own prospects, own claims, own statements, own alerts. Never a refusal's internal reason, its evidence or note, another seller's claim, or a customer relationship the seller did not establish.
identities.KAURO_OWNER: The Kauro owner across workspaces, under the owner's assurance; owner-only reads live under /api/v1/ops. The cross-workspace scope and its RLS are Order 15's.

items.title: "Clean your data" runs the free check, plan, approval and quote with no target contract

outcomes.meaning: a HUBSPOT or SALESFORCE project's audit names no targetContractId; nothing was written (until CP-02 the closed schema answered SCHEMA_VIOLATION REQUIRED, with the same status)
a CLEAN project's audit names a targetContractId: CLEAN binds the one canonical CLEAN target hash and takes no target contract; nothing was written, no grant reserved, no provider called

rules: The project's mode (server-held, CMD011) decides the branch; no request member, header or hash chooses it.

CLEAN: no targetContractId; the audit records CLEAN_ONLY_TARGET_HASH (plan-compiler.ts) as targetContractHash and locks no target row; CreatePlan, ApprovePlan and CreateQuote bind that hash for CLEAN and never read a target contract.
HUBSPOT and SALESFORCE: unchanged, a confirmed and current target contract of the project is required (TARGET_STALE when it is not current).
The quote of a CLEAN project shows no target fingerprint (Quote has no target member; QuoteView unchanged).

Order 16's text named the CLEAN refusal "422 TARGET_NOT_APPLICABLE" and said a HUBSPOT project without a target is "still TARGET_STALE". Order 17 keeps the token as the reason but answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST, as CMD011 already does for TARGET_INSTANCE_REQUIRED (the repository's convention for a mode-dependent member), and keeps today's 400 for a missing CRM target: a client that branches on the status sees no change. TARGET_STALE stays for a target that is given but not current.

acceptance.title: CLEAN audit without a target contract
acceptance.scenario: A sealed revision of a CLEAN project starts an audit with no targetContractId.
acceptance.expected: The audit is queued, binds CLEAN_ONLY_TARGET_HASH as its target hash and locks no target contract row; audit.queued.v1 carries no targetContractId.

acceptance.title: CLEAN reaches a quote with no target contract
acceptance.scenario: A CLEAN project goes from the free check to CreatePlan, ApprovePlan and CreateQuote without ever creating a target contract.
acceptance.expected: Plan.targetContractHash and Approval.targetContractHash are the canonical CLEAN hash; the quote is issued and shows no target fingerprint; no TARGET_STALE is raised anywhere on the path.

acceptance.title: A target supplied for CLEAN is refused
acceptance.scenario: A CLEAN project's StartAudit names a targetContractId (valid, current or not).
acceptance.expected: 400 INVALID_REQUEST TARGET_NOT_APPLICABLE; no audit, no grant reservation, no provider call, no event.

acceptance.title: HubSpot and Salesforce still need their target
acceptance.scenario: A HUBSPOT and a SALESFORCE project start an audit without targetContractId, then with a superseded one.
acceptance.expected: 400 INVALID_REQUEST TARGET_CONTRACT_REQUIRED, then 422 TARGET_STALE; nothing written in either case.

acceptance.title: No request can choose the CLEAN path
acceptance.scenario: A HUBSPOT project's audit omits the target and adds unknown members (mode, targetContractHash) or replays a CLEAN audit's idempotency key.
acceptance.expected: The closed schema refuses unknown members; the omission is TARGET_CONTRACT_REQUIRED; a replay under another body is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a CLEAN plan never binds a CRM target and a CRM plan never binds the CLEAN hash.

eventPayloadChanges.note: a CLEAN audit omits targetContractId and carries targetContractHash = CLEAN_ONLY_TARGET_HASH; AUDIT_ORCHESTRATION reads it as optional

items.title: The project dates read: five dates kept apart, never summed

contracts.name: ProjectDate
contracts.flow: Quote, retention records, extension and hold → the project dates read
contracts.invariant: One date of one kind with its own rule; a date is never derived by adding another kind's period, and an estimate is never shown as a commitment.
fields: Which of the five dates (F-24); PENDING_PAYMENT_HOLD is reserved (the item's reservation) and NOT_APPLICABLE until CP-02.17 is active.
NOT_APPLICABLE: no anchor yet or not offered; AVAILABLE: may be requested (extension); RUNNING; ENDED; USED: the one extension was granted.
The date itself, when the anchor exists.
Retention kinds only: the absolute maximum the record allows (14 days from sealing, 17 with the UNPAID extension under CP-01.02).
The policy key that sets the date, e.g. pricing.quoteDays or retention.unpaidDaysFromReady.
The version the date was computed under: pricing.scheduleVersion or the record's retention label.
The fact the date counts from.
The quote, retention record, extension or hold the date is read from.
What may be done about this date now; RECORD_TRANSFER_PROOF only after CP-02.17.
Who may do it (the command's registry role; Order 15 enforces it).

contracts.name: ProjectDates
contracts.flow: Project, quote and retention journals → agency screens (Quote, Payment, Overview, Projects, Data and deletion, Billing)
contracts.invariant: Exactly one entry per kind, in the order of the kind enum; the governing retention kind names which date deletes the data, it never adds two dates.
fields: The five dates, one per kind.
The retention date that currently governs deletion (the later of extension and hold, never their sum).

SourceRevisionView.retention[] stays as it is; this read adds the extension and the project-level view.

acceptance.scenario: A sealed UNPAID project with an issued quote, read through GetProjectDates.
acceptance.expected: Five entries in kind order; QUOTE_PRICE_VALIDITY and FREE_CHECK_RETENTION carry different dates and rules; EXTENSION is AVAILABLE for the owner or an admin; PENDING_PAYMENT_HOLD is NOT_APPLICABLE; PAID_RETENTION is NOT_APPLICABLE.

acceptance.scenario: A project whose extension was used and, after CP-02.17, whose hold is running.
acceptance.expected: governingRetentionKind names the later of the two; no entry's date equals one period added to another; no member carries a total.

items.title: The one extension for the free check, to an exceptional 17 days: response, errors and the extension contract

contracts.name: RetentionExtension
contracts.flow: RequestRetentionExtension (CMD060) → scheduler, dates read and restore journal
contracts.invariant: One per project across every retention class; it never revives expired data, and only an UNPAID record's extension may move its hard deadline, to at most the policy's UNPAID ceiling from sealing.
fields: Hard deadline after (moves for UNPAID only).
The most the extension could reach: the hard deadline for paid classes, sealing plus retention.extendHardCapExceptions.UNPAID.ceilingDaysFromSeal for UNPAID.

schema.description: The most the extension could reach.

outcomes.meaning: the project has no ACTIVE retention record with a soft deadline in an extendable class (UNPAID, PAID_ORDINARY, PAID_STAGED); an unpaid source is extendable once the backend writes its soft deadline (7 days from ready)
the soft deadline is already at the ceiling (the hard cap, or for UNPAID sealing plus 17 days); nothing is granted and the extension is not consumed
the project already used its one extension, in any class: an extension used on the free check leaves none for the paid project; nothing resets a clock

rules: UNPAID: soft = min(previous soft + granted, seal + 17 days); the hard deadline moves to that value; without an extension nothing changes (14 days).
Paid classes: unchanged; the hard deadline never moves.
One extension per project across classes, enforced by the existing uniqueness (kauro.retention_extensions).
A restored backup never revives data whose period ended; the extension is a journaled authority fact (retention_record.extended.v1 → AUTHORITY_JOURNAL).
NO_EXTENDABLE_RECORD keeps its token: its meaning narrows once the backend writes the UNPAID soft deadline; until then an UNPAID-only project still receives it.

acceptance.title: Free check without extension: 14 days
acceptance.scenario: An UNPAID revision sealed at T, ready at T+1d, no extension.
acceptance.expected: Soft deadline T+8d (7 from ready), hard deadline T+14d; the sweeper deletes at the effective deadline.

acceptance.title: Free check with the extension: at most 17 days
acceptance.scenario: The same revision; the owner requests 259200 s on day 12.
acceptance.expected: Granted capped at T+17d (cappedAtHardDeadline true, ceilingRule UNPAID_EXCEPTIONAL_CEILING, hardDeadline T+17d); never later.

acceptance.title: One extension per project across classes, under concurrency
acceptance.scenario: Two concurrent requests on the free check, then a request after purchase on the paid record.
acceptance.expected: One wins; the other is EXTENSION_ALREADY_USED; the paid request is EXTENSION_ALREADY_USED; no second row.

acceptance.title: No extension after the soft deadline or of a deleted scope
acceptance.scenario: A request one second after the soft deadline; a request on a DELETING record.
acceptance.expected: SOFT_DEADLINE_PASSED; RETENTION_EXPIRED; nothing written.

acceptance.title: A restore never revives extended data
acceptance.scenario: A backup taken on day 15 restored on day 18 for a revision extended to day 17.
acceptance.expected: The restore journal applies the deletion before traffic; no byte of the revision is readable.

commands.name: WithdrawConsent
commands.precondition: The record is the caller's own, GIVEN and of an optional kind (MARKETING_COMMUNICATIONS).

commands.failure: Another person's record answers as not found; DATA_PROCESSING_AUTHORIZATION and PRIVACY_NOTICE_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT are not withdrawn here: the refusal names the rights procedure of the Policy.

rules: Four different things, never confused: consent for commercial communications (this item, optional, per channel), the authorization to process data for the service (this item, required at registration, revoked only through the rights procedure), an authenticated session (proof of who calls, never consent) and step-up assurance for sensitive operations (proof of recent presence, never consent).
